checked_claims.note: Re-derived independently rather than accepted. Under the packet CE convention deg(W_f|_C)=4g+12-4f gives deg W_5=16, deg L=6, chi(L)=1, so h^0(L)=1+h^0(omega_C^2 tensor W_5^vee) with the auxiliary bundle of degree 4; (N) pins W_5=omega_C^2(-D), hence h^0(L)=1+h^0(D) and Clifford plus the (CE)+(BAL) hyperelliptic exclusion force h^0(D)=2, i.e. h^0(L)=3 and h^1(L)=2. This is exactly CLM-0088-3 (with CLM-0088-2 for the hyperelliptic branch), dual-confirmed by REV-0139/REV-0142; CLM-0086-2 independently supplies the same fibrewise value and the Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle statement in the Abel-Jacobi fibre-product model that this artifact actually uses. Surjectivity of U->S was re-checked from scratch: the fixed part of |L| has degree at most one (Clifford on the moving part), the moving part is base-point-free, and in characteristic zero a general member is reduced and avoids the fixed point, so every geometric fibre carries six pairwise distinct points; base-point-freeness of L is nowhere required. Smoothness and pure relative dimension two are immediate from openness in a P^2-bundle plus fibrewise nonemptiness.

Numerics re-derived: deg W_4=20, deg W_5=16, deg W=36, h^1(W)=0 (both pieces exceed 2g-2=10), so h^0(W)=36-10=26 and pi_{B*}W_B is locally free of rank 26 with base change; Gamma is finite flat of degree six and W has rank two, so the target has rank 12; Fit_0 of the cokernel of a map into a rank-12 bundle is I_12 by definition. Corank at most one because coker(phi)=coker(phi_5) (the two vanishings deg W_4=20>10 and deg W_4-6=14>10 hold) and its fibres are Serre-dual to H^0 of N=omega tensor W_5^vee(Gamma) of degree 10-16+6=0, which is nonzero only for the trivial bundle; hence I_11 has empty vanishing locus and I_j=O_B for j<=11 since minor ideals decrease. The Fitting identity I_12=a_N^*I_e is CLM-0065-4/CLM-0065-9 specialized in CLM-0088-6, whose six-disjoint-sections hypothesis is met exactly because the base is Conf_6(C/S). I independently checked the intrinsic-derivative mechanism: at e the kernel is H^0(omega) of dimension g=6 and the cokernel H^1(omega) of dimension 1, and the derivative is the perfect Serre pairing, so the maximal-minor ideal is the full maximal ideal of e and pulls back correctly (Fitting ideals commute with base change). Reducedness of S is not needed for this clause, which is consistent with the recorded ATT-0088 scope.

Independently reconstructed: since a_N factors as B -> Hilb^6(C/S) -> Pic^6(C/S), the Fitting subscheme Z=a_N^{-1}(e) equals B x_{Hilb^6} AJ scheme-theoretically, and Conf_6(C/S) -> Hilb^6(C/S) is finite etale of degree 720 onto the distinct-support open; base change of a finite etale S_6-torsor gives Z=Ord(U) -> U finite etale of degree 720, hence Z->S smooth surjective of pure relative dimension two. This is CLM-0066-6 combined with CLM-0088-8, both dual-confirmed. FND-0075's coarse-moduli caveat does not bite here because the base is a fixed family C/S and no quotient by curve automorphisms is taken; no stack-versus-coarse or invariants-versus-coinvariants issue arises in this statement.

Verified independently of the dependency text: Z->S and U->S are smooth, hence flat, so generizations lift and the generic point of every irreducible component maps to a generic point of S; fibres are pure of dimension two, so for S of finite type over k the function-field transcendence-degree computation gives dim Z_beta = dim S_alpha + 2, and likewise for U. Matches the finite-type clause of CLM-0088-8. The clause correctly asserts nothing about the number of components or monodromy orbits.

Z is closed in B by the Fitting presentation; Z->S is smooth of relative dimension two (clause 3) and B=Conf_6(C/S)->S is smooth of relative dimension six, so the closed immersion is regular of codimension four with locally free rank-four conormal sheaf. The route matters and is the correct one: regularity is deduced from S-smoothness of source and target, not from any expected-versus-actual determinantal codimension comparison, so FND-0068's blocked inference is not used. I probed the reverse worry as well - a_N^*I_e is generated locally by six pullbacks of generators of the codimension-six ideal of the identity section while Z has codimension four - and it is not an obstruction: an ideal of height four may be generated by six elements and still be locally generated by a regular sequence of length four. Matches CLM-0088-9.

finding_candidates.statement: At (g,n)=(6,6) the whole rank and minor-ideal package of the balanced CE evaluation is blind to the CE line-bundle convention, so it cannot be used to disambiguate a statement that says only 'the canonical filtered relations bundle'. Reading W as gamma^*F with its Harder-Narasimhan filtration (sub gamma^*O(5) of degree 20, quotient gamma^*O(4) of degree 16) gives exactly the same numerical data as the packet convention W=i^*(O_X(2) tensor p^*F^vee) (sub W_4 of degree 20, quotient W_5 of degree 16): deg W=36, h^1(W)=0, h^0(W)=26, restriction to a degree-six Gamma of rank 12, twist N=omega tensor W_5^vee(Gamma) of degree 10-16+6=0, both ATT-0065 inequalities d_4-n>2g-2 and d_5-n=2g-2 satisfied, hence fibre rank 11 or 12, I_j=O_B for j<=11 and Fit_0=a_N^*I_e verbatim. The readings diverge only in L: the packet gives L=omega_C(-D) with h^0=3, the naive reading gives L'=4D-K=L tensor (5D-2K), and h^0(L')=1+h^0(2K-4D) equals 3 only if 5D is isomorphic to 2K, which no stated hypothesis supplies. Consequence for the campaign: the h^0(L)=3 clause, not the rank table, is the convention check, and any downstream statement invoking W_4/W_5 must restate W_f=(O_X(2) tensor gamma^*O(-f))|_C rather than rely on numerics to pin it.

ATT-0104 states its five conclusions for gamma:C->P^1_S, a trivial P^1-bundle, whereas its own dependency ATT-0088 proves the same conclusions for gamma:C->P with s:P->S an arbitrary P^1-bundle (and needs S reduced only for the Part III clauses). The narrowing is sound but reduces applicability: over the universal balanced tetragonal base the tetragonal map is determined only up to PGL_2, so the natural target is a P^1-bundle or a PGL_2-quotient stack that need not be Zariski-trivial. Nodes C66-TATE-SUPPORT and C66-CEX-LOCAL should therefore quote CLM-0088-8/CLM-0088-9 (or record the descent, cf. FND-0127 for the scheme-to-stack half) rather than this lemma when working over the universal family. Two traps to avoid when doing so: the narrowing is not needed for global existence of L, since E and F are bundles on the target and X=P_P(E^vee) carries a canonical global O_X(1), so W, W_5 and L are global for any P^1-bundle target and no Severi-Brauer obstruction to Zariski-local triviality of the P^2-bundle arises; and the residual twist of L by a line bundle pulled back from the base is invisible in Pic_{C/S}, so the Abel-Jacobi section is canonical even though L is not.

Evidence for FND-0107 in the balanced (6,6) setting, with the global-versus-local step made explicit. When h^0(L_s) is constant (here equal to 3 by CLM-0088-3), the Abel-Jacobi fibre product Hilb^6(C/S) x_{Pic^6(C/S)} S and the projective bundle P_S(pi_*L) are canonically isomorphic over all of S, not merely fibrewise: the fibre product's T-points impose the Picard condition only locally on T, but for a relative divisor Gamma with O(Gamma) locally isomorphic to L_T twisted from T, the sheaf pi_{T*}(O(Gamma) tensor L_T^{-1}) is invertible (fibrewise h^0 of the trivial bundle equals one, so base change applies) and the canonical map from its pullback is an isomorphism, producing a global twist M. Hence an artifact may substitute either model for the other in this regime, but only after recording constancy of h^0; without constancy the fibre-product model is the correct one and the projective-bundle model is not.

strongest_attack:
Identity checks first: the artifact's packet_id, packet_sha256 (e8bc3dbc...) and packet_binding_sha256 (76cc8a6d...) match TASK.json, its target dictionary is field-for-field identical to the task target, and its theorem_statement is the task's verbatim. (ATT-0088 carries an older packet_sha256 under the same binding hash, consistent with findings appended to the packet after it was written; the binding hash is what governs.) The listed adversarial axes are mostly vacuous against this artifact by construction: it makes no cohomological, Borel-Moore, Poincare-duality, Tate-twist, Gysin, Kunneth, spectral-sequence, semisimplification or motivic claim, no statement about M_{6,6} or coarse moduli, and no integral-coefficient or stable-pair assertion, so there is no degree/twist bookkeeping to falsify and no predicted motive used as a theorem; it also correctly declines the monodromy, stabilizer and component-count claims that FND-0053, FND-0086 and FND-0098 would otherwise reach.

Strongest attack attempted: the referent of 'the canonical filtered relations bundle'. The statement never defines W, and there are two live readings. On the naive reading W=gamma^*F with its Harder-Narasimhan filtration, the sub is gamma^*O(5) of degree 20 and the quotient gamma^*O(4) of degree 16 - exactly the same degree pair as the packet convention W=i^*(O_X(2) tensor p^*F^vee). I checked that this wrong reading satisfies clause (2) in full: deg W=36, h^1(W)=0, h^0(W)=26, target rank 12, N of degree 10-16+6=0 so fibre rank 11 or 12, I_j=O_B for j<=11, and Fit_0=a_N^*I_e via the same ATT-0065 hypotheses. It fails only in clause (1): the naive L'=gamma^*O(4) tensor omega^{-1}=4D-K equals the packet L=omega_C(-D) only if 5D is isomorphic to 2K, and h^0(L')=1+h^0(2K-4D) is then not 3. So had the naive reading been intended, clause (1) would be false and the verdict refuted. The attack fails because the packet's normative CE line-bundle convention (which explicitly warns that W_5 'is not the O_{P1}(5) summand of F'), FND-0097's degree-20-sub / degree-16-quotient description, and CLM-0065-5 all fix the referent, and the artifact is hash-bound to that packet. It survives as a statement-hygiene defect and as finding candidate FC-C66-CE-CONVENTION-RANK-BLIND.

Second attack: the artifact silently swaps models. Its AJ is the fibre product Hilb^6(C/S) x_{Pic^6(C/S)} S, whereas the clause actually proved in CLM-0088-8 concerns AJ=P_S(pi_*L); moreover the statement never names the section S -> Pic^6 (it must be the class of L) and uses a_N and I_e without defining them. This fails as a refutation on three grounds: the fibre-product model with its Zariski-local-triviality conclusion is proved directly in CLM-0086-2 and fixed as the correct model in CLM-0066-5, both dual-confirmed; the two functors agree here because h^0(L_s)=3 is constant (so Grauert applies) and pi_*(O(Gamma) tensor L^{-1}) is invertible, upgrading the 'locally on T' Picard condition to a global M; and the [L]-section is canonical because the residual twist ambiguity of L by a line bundle pulled back from S dies in Pic_{C/S}. Note also that the twist ambiguity does not produce a Severi-Brauer form: E and F are honest bundles on the target and X=P_P(E^vee) carries a global O_X(1), so W_5 and L exist globally and 'Zariski-locally trivial' is legitimate rather than merely etale-locally trivial. a_N and I_e are standard campaign notation from CLM-0065-4.

Third attack: clause (5) against the six-generator presentation. a_N^*I_e is locally generated by six functions while Z has codimension four, and the Abel-Jacobi map is not submersive along Z (its fibre jumps from a point to a P^2 exactly at [L]); one might hope to force a non-regular immersion. This fails: regularity is obtained from S-smoothness of Z and of B, not from generator counts or determinantal expectation, and height-four ideals with six generators are routinely generated by regular sequences of length four; the scheme-theoretic fibre of Abel-Jacobi over [L] is the honest linear system P(H^0(L)), smooth of dimension two, so the jump does not damage the Fitting scheme structure.

I also re-derived, without leaning on the dependency text, the (6,6) degree table, chi(L)=1, the Clifford/hyperelliptic exclusion route to h^0(L)=3, fibrewise existence of a reduced member of |L| in characteristic zero even when |L| has a base point, the finite-etale degree-720 ordering comparison, and the flat-generization component argument. Everything matched. Verdict confirmed for the stated lemma only: it is a faithful, slightly narrowed corollary of dual-confirmed inputs, it discharges nothing of RED-0001, and it asserts no Hodge, weight or Tate conclusion, so confirming it does not advance the campaign target.
theorem_statement: Relative balanced ordered-incidence theorem. Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and S a reduced locally Noetherian k-scheme. Let pi:C->S be a smooth proper family of geometrically connected genus-six curves and gamma:C->P^1_S a finite flat degree-four cover carrying the standard Casnati-Ekedahl ideal resolution (CE), with relations bundle fibrewise F_s isomorphic to O(4)+O(5). Assume the weak relative-canonical normalization (N) fibrewise. Let 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 be the canonical filtered relations bundle, put L=W_5 tensor omega_{C/S}^{-1}, let B=Conf_6(C/S), let Gamma be its universal ordered divisor, and let phi:pi_{B*}W_B->pi_{B*}(W_B|Gamma) be the intrinsic evaluation map. Define Z=V(Fit_0(coker phi)) inside B, let AJ=Hilb^6(C/S) times_{Pic^6(C/S)} S, and let U be the distinct-support open of AJ. Then: (1) h^0(L_s)=3 and h^1(L_s)=2 for every geometric s, AJ is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle over S, and U->S is smooth, surjective, and purely of relative dimension two; (2) phi has ranks 26->12, every geometric fibre has rank 11 or 12, I_j(phi)=O_B for j<=11, and I_12(phi)=Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e scheme-theoretically; (3) forgetting the ordering identifies Z canonically with the S_6-torsor Ord(U)->U, which is finite etale of degree 720, so Z->S is smooth and surjective of pure relative dimension two; (4) if S is of finite type, every irreducible component of Z and of U dominates an irreducible component of S and has dimension equal to the dimension of that component plus two; and (5) Z->B is a regular immersion of pure codimension four with locally free rank-four conormal sheaf. No assertion is made about the number of components, geometric monodromy, stabilizers, a morphism to M_{6,6}, or unbalanced Casnati-Ekedahl strata.
